pr.title: Mark items done and switch between open, done and all

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_done.sql adds done NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with a CHECK. test/done.test.js 'AC-1' checks that the seeded rows are all 0 after the migrations run and that done=2 is rejected.
src/index.js filters on done = 0 and orders by id. 'AC-2' checks both / and /?view=open.
'AC-3' marks ids 3 and 1 done and expects ['✓ First item','✓ Third item'], which checks the filter, the order and the ✓ mark.
'AC-4' expects the full list in id order with only the done item marked.
'AC-5' asserts the exact nav HTML for each view and for /. The current view is a <strong>, not a link.
'AC-6' checks that Open, closed, an empty value and __proto__ give 400 with no <li>. Object.hasOwn guards the lookup.
'AC-7' checks Nothing open., Nothing done yet. and No items yet. for every view on an empty table. The extra COUNT query handles the empty-table case.

traffic/routes.json lists /?view=done and /?view=all. The 'AC-8' test checks them. traffic/src/index.js fetches ROUTES as given, and the traffic tests use ROUTES with a fake app that now records the query.

lenses.note: The spec has a go dated 2026-10-12. Both decisions are followed: the default view is open and the view is a query parameter. Nothing is added beyond the spec except the traffic-check regex change, which the spec's AC-8 needs and the PR discloses.

All 8 acceptance items are met. Each of the 6 state-table rows has a test in the 'states' describe block, and the empty-table row is also covered in every view by AC-7. No acceptance item was edited after the go.

The tests assert behaviour: the list contents, the status codes and the exact nav HTML. The fake app in test/traffic.test.js was widened to record the query, which the PR discloses. tests/traffic-config.test.sh covers a query route passing and refuses a fragment or space. I did not run the tests here; CI does.
The README describes the open, done and all views. The spec is added. I found nothing stale.

The view parameter is checked with Object.hasOwn before use, so __proto__ is rejected. The SQL fragments come from a constant table, not from user input. The empty-table fallback runs a second query only when the result is empty.
Titles are still HTML-escaped. The view value is allow-listed and never echoed back. The 400 body is a fixed string. I found no planted instructions in the repository content.
The change adds a plain HTML nav and list markup but no CSS or components; there are no screenshots, so there was no visual design to review.
No browser flow was run, because the change has no preview. The tests cover the views and the nav HTML.

The title is under 72 characters and describes the observable change. The body's claims match the diff: the 400 on any other view, the traffic-check change, and the fake-app change. There are no assets commits to check.
